http_semantics.note: No 2xx masking: every disposition was an honest 5xx with an error body. Notable for the auditor's fifth criterion: the 9 request-side-decidable malformed bodies (string/number/boolean/array/nested objects) returned the same 500 'Service internal error' as the perfectly legal documented no-body control — the status code does not discriminate input validity at all because the handler never reads the body; a 4xx family response never occurs on this endpoint under any input.

contract_grounding.assertion_text_quoted: returns 200 ok; intended for use only when quorum is permanently lost
contract_grounding.note: violates=true on the observed deployment: the request form is exactly the documented bodyless control, squarely inside the quote's domain, and the API returned 500 where the assertion promises 200 — this is not the ambiguous 'accepted-but-maybe-compliant' case. Caveat the auditor must weigh: the 200 promise was exercised on a standalone deployment (GET /cluster status:'disabled'); the doc documents no distributed-mode precondition, so the constraint text itself carries no such condition. The quoted text is the verbatim description field of assertion qdrant_behavioral_cluster_recover_001 in structured_contract.json (whose companion expected_behavior field reads: HTTP 200 on cluster recovery (dangerous operational op)).

source_grounding.call_chain_traced: POST /cluster/recover -> recover_current_peer (src/actix/api/cluster_api.rs:60-73; handler signature has no body parameter, so all 9 body variants are invisible to it) -> auth.check_global_access(manage) passes -> toc.request_snapshot() (lib/storage/src/content_manager/toc/mod.rs:546-551) -> get_consensus_proposal_sender() (toc/mod.rs:775-779) -> consensus_proposal_sender is None on this deployment because main.rs:508-514 sets it to None when settings.cluster.enabled=false (comment: 'We don't need sender for the single-node mode') -> StorageError::service_error("Qdrant is running in standalone mode") -> helpers.rs:247 maps ServiceError to 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR -> observed body 'Service internal error: Qdrant is running in standalone mode' (errors.rs:21 template). Fully deterministic; no gRPC/tonic face for this operation exists.
source_grounding.verification_note: A precondition guard EXISTS in source and fires deterministically: get_consensus_proposal_sender() rejects with a typed, descriptive service error when running standalone — this is not a missing check, not a panic, and not silent acceptance. It is NOT marked by_design_in_source because no comment or docstring declares the endpoint's 500-on-standalone disposition intentional; the only intent-comment found (main.rs:512 'We don't need sender for the single-node mode') documents the None-sender design at the construction site, one step removed from the endpoint disposition. Whether 'typed 500 ServiceError for an inapplicable deployment mode, on an endpoint whose docs document only 200 and no preconditions' is an acceptable design or a doc/behavior contract gap is left to the auditor.

mundane_explanation.surviving: deployment-mode precondition: the sandbox runs a single-node deployment (GET /cluster -> status:'disabled', i.e. settings.cluster.enabled=false). POST /cluster/recover is a consensus-only operation and the source guards it to fail with 'Qdrant is running in standalone mode'. The v1.18.x documentation documents neither this precondition nor any error response for the endpoint, so the assertion's 200 promise is unachievable on any standalone deployment while the doc gives no warning. This deployment-mode/undocumented-precondition defense survives mechanical exclusion and is the auditor's central by-design-vs-doc-gap question.
